newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan shilling weaker vs dlr on political concern.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan shilling weaker vs dlr on political concern.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling was a touch weaker against the dollar on Monday, and commercial bank dealers said it could weaken further as the market begins to feel the effect of election jitters ahead of polls sometime this year.
"We saw some foreign investors pull out of the market on Friday. They are now buying back their dollars instead of re-investing them in treasury bills," one dealer said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 53.47 against the dollar from 53.46 on Friday, while against the pound it was posted at a commercial mean of 87.61 from 87.67.
Dealers said rolling over the treasury bills meant tying up funds for the next three months, a risk which foreign investors were not prepared to take in an election year.
"It's not going to happen all at once, but they've already begun pulling out of the market," one dealer said.

"The underlying tone right now is for a weaker shilling," one dealer said. He said part of the reason was because investors had rushed in to cash in on the shilling's sharp appreciation from 53.87 on Thursday to 53.46 on Friday.
The money market remained firm with overnight rates quoted at 20 percent unchanged. Dealers said they expected a tighter market in view of tax payments due on Tuesday.
